title: Best LinkedIn Prospecting Tools Without Sales Navigator
summary: Compare the best LinkedIn prospecting tools without Sales Navigator: Apollo, Hunter, PhantomBuster, Clay, and Orange Slice — with costs and trade-offs.
body_markdown:
## What Are the Best LinkedIn Prospecting Tools Without Sales Navigator?


The best tools for LinkedIn prospecting without Sales Navigator are **Apollo.io** , **Hunter.io** , **PhantomBuster** , **Clay** , and **Orange Slice** . Each one gives you access to LinkedIn intelligence — job titles, company data, verified contact info — without paying for a Sales Navigator seat. Which one fits depends on your volume, your workflow, and how much signal you need beyond a name and an email.


Sales Navigator costs hundreds of dollars per seat per year. According to LinkedIn's published pricing, individual Sales Navigator Core seats are priced at $99.99/month billed monthly. For an early-stage founder or a lean SDR team, that budget is often better spent on outreach tooling or additional data coverage. The tools below cover the same core use case: find the right person, at the right company, with a way to reach them.


---


## How Does LinkedIn Prospecting Work Without Sales Navigator?


LinkedIn itself doesn't expose its data through a public API for prospecting. Every tool on this list works around that in one of three ways:


1. **Pre-built contact databases** indexed from LinkedIn and other public sources (Apollo, Hunter, ZoomInfo)
2. **Browser-based scrapers** that automate your own LinkedIn session to extract profiles (PhantomBuster, Dux-Soup)
3. **AI research agents** that combine LinkedIn intelligence with web research, firmographics, and signal data to build enriched lists on demand (Orange Slice, Clay)


Each approach has a different risk profile, cost structure, and data freshness trade-off.


---


## The Tools, Compared


### Apollo.io


Apollo is the most common Sales Navigator alternative for SDR teams. Its database covers over 275 million contacts across 73 million companies, according to[Apollo's own product documentation](https://www.apollo.io/) . You can filter by job title, seniority, company size, industry, location, and technology used. The free tier includes a limited number of email exports per month; paid plans scale the volume significantly.


**What it does well:** Bulk list building, built-in sequencing, CRM integrations, and a Chrome extension for single-contact lookups on LinkedIn profiles.


**Where it falls short:** Data freshness varies. Contacts who changed jobs recently are often stale. Run any Apollo export through an email verifier before importing to a sequence tool — a bounce rate above 3% will damage your sending domain's reputation.


---


### Hunter.io


Hunter is purpose-built for finding and verifying email addresses. You can search by company domain to surface all indexed contacts, or use the LinkedIn integration to find an email for a specific profile. It's not a list-building tool in the same way Apollo is, but it's the most reliable single-contact lookup available at its price point.


[Hunter's published accuracy data](https://hunter.io/email-verifier) states that its email verifier checks against mail server responses, syntax, and domain validity — returning a confidence score rather than a binary result.


**What it does well:** High deliverability confidence on the emails it returns. The domain search is useful for mapping out all known contacts at a target account.


**Where it falls short:** No firmographic filtering, no phone numbers, no sequencing. It's a data point tool, not a prospecting workflow.


---


### PhantomBuster


PhantomBuster runs automations — "Phantoms" — through your own LinkedIn session. You give it a LinkedIn search URL or a list of profile URLs, and it extracts names, titles, companies, and sometimes contact info at scale. There are Phantoms for LinkedIn Search, Sales Navigator (if you have it), LinkedIn Groups, event attendees, and more.


According to[PhantomBuster's documentation](https://phantombuster.com/phantoms) , the platform offers over 100 pre-built automation templates across LinkedIn, Sales Navigator, and other platforms.


**What it does well:** Flexibility. If you can navigate to a LinkedIn list, PhantomBuster can scrape it. Good for niche lists like conference speakers, group members, or people who liked a specific post.


**Where it falls short:** It uses your own LinkedIn session, so aggressive use risks account restriction. Keep daily volumes conservative. The extracted data is raw — you still need to enrich it with emails separately.


---


### Clay


Clay is a spreadsheet-style enrichment platform that connects to dozens of data providers simultaneously. You bring a list of names and companies, and Clay runs them through multiple enrichment sources in sequence — a waterfall approach — to maximize coverage. It has a LinkedIn data integration and a built-in AI research layer.


[Clay's documentation](https://www.clay.com/) describes integrations with over 75 data providers, making it one of the broadest enrichment waterfalls available without building a custom stack.


**What it does well:** Waterfall enrichment across providers, AI-written personalization at scale, and highly customizable column logic. Strong choice for teams that want to build complex enrichment workflows.


**Where it falls short:** The learning curve is steep. Getting full value out of Clay requires meaningful setup time and some technical comfort. It's also credit-heavy if you run large lists through multiple enrichment steps.


---


### Orange Slice


[Orange Slice](https://www.orangeslice.ai/) is a chat-first smart spreadsheet for B2B prospecting. You describe your ICP in plain English — "Series A SaaS companies in the US with 50–200 employees hiring a Head of Sales" — and columns auto-populate from LinkedIn intelligence, verified emails, phone numbers, firmographics, funding data, tech stack, and hiring signals.


It's built for SDRs, founders doing their own outbound, and RevOps teams who want a full prospecting workflow without stitching together five separate tools. A natural-language browser agent can scrape any site, not just LinkedIn. Credits are charged only when data is actually found, so you don't pay for blanks.


**What it does well:** End-to-end list building from ICP description to enriched, export-ready spreadsheet. Direct integrations with HubSpot, Salesforce, Instantly, and CSV. TypeScript columns for custom scoring logic. The[lead generation agent](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/lead-generation-agent) handles the full find-and-enrich loop in one place.


**Where it falls short:** Orange Slice is not a sequencing tool. It builds and enriches the list; you still need a separate tool to send the emails. It also doesn't replace a CRM — it feeds one. See[pricing](https://www.orangeslice.ai/pricing) for credit costs.

## How Do You Build a LinkedIn Prospect List Without Sales Navigator?


Here's a repeatable workflow that doesn't require a Sales Navigator subscription:


**Step 1: Define your ICP precisely.** Title, seniority, company size, industry, geography, and any signal filters (hiring, funding, tech stack). Vague ICPs produce bloated lists with low conversion.


**Step 2: Build the raw list.** Use Apollo for broad coverage, PhantomBuster for niche LinkedIn lists (group members, event attendees), or Orange Slice if you want to generate the list from a plain-English ICP description.


**Step 3: Enrich contact data.** If your list-building tool doesn't return verified emails, run it through Hunter or use a waterfall enrichment layer. A list with a bounce rate above 3% will get your domain flagged.


**Step 4: Layer in signals.** Hiring data, funding rounds, and tech stack tell you *when* to reach out, not just *who* to reach. The[data enrichment agent](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/data-enrichment-agent) can append these signals to an existing list.


**Step 5: Score and prioritize.** Not every contact on a list deserves equal attention. Use ICP fit criteria to tier your list before it hits a sequence. The[lead qualification agent](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/lead-qualification-agent) can automate this step.


**Step 6: Export to your stack.** Push to HubSpot, Salesforce, or your cold email tool. Keep your CRM clean by avoiding duplicate imports — the[CRM agent](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/crm-agent) handles deduplication and sync.


---


## When Is Sales Navigator Actually Worth It?


Be honest about this. Sales Navigator earns its cost in specific situations:


- **Large enterprise AE teams** who need TeamLink for warm intro paths through their company's network
- **Account-based programs** where saved account lists with real-time update alerts are critical
- **Complex Boolean search** inside LinkedIn's full database, including profile text and past employers


For most SDRs at growth-stage companies, and for most founders doing their own outbound, the tools above cover the use case at a fraction of the cost. The gap between Sales Navigator and a well-configured Apollo + enrichment workflow is smaller than LinkedIn's pricing suggests.


---


## Which Tool Should You Choose for Your Workflow?


If you need one recommendation: start with **Apollo** for list volume and **Orange Slice** for ICP-driven list generation with enrichment baked in. They serve different moments in the same workflow. Apollo gives you a broad database to filter; Orange Slice lets you describe what you want and get back a spreadsheet that's already enriched and ready to export.


For teams building more complex plays — multi-step sequences triggered by signals, enriched lists routed to different reps by ICP tier — the[workflows page](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/workflows) shows how those automations connect. The[use cases page](https://www.orangeslice.ai/use-cases) has concrete plays worth borrowing.


Pick the simplest stack that gets you to a verified, enriched, export-ready list. Add complexity only when a specific gap appears in your process.
